empty.appearance: No pack options yet (e.g. CustomArmor, Color).
empty.data: No item data yet (e.g. Food, Equippable).
empty.settings: No settings yet (e.g. Tags, Fuel Time).
empty.blockSettings: No block settings yet (e.g. Hardness, Sounds, Loot).
empty.blockBehavior: No behavior options yet (e.g. sounds, extra behaviors).

properties.premiumHint: Only CraftEngine Premium reads this property.
properties.tooLow: This property requires Minecraft {min} or newer. Your project is set to {version}.
properties.tooHigh: This property only exists up to Minecraft {max}.

general.title: Basics
general.description: Name, ID and base material of the item
general.idEmpty: The ID must not be empty.
general.idInvalid: Only lowercase letters, numbers and _ are allowed.
general.idDuplicate: This ID is already used by “{name}”.
general.idRepeated: This ID is used by several of the new items.
general.materialHelp: Base item in Minecraft. Default is PAPER; for tools/armor use the matching material.
general.tooltipHelp: Without its own color, Minecraft shows the lore purple and italic.

yaml.extraDescription: For everything the editor doesn’t offer (yet). Applied last on top of the settings and overrides identical keys.
yaml.keyHint: Don’t include the item key ({id}) – only the content below it.
yaml.finalDescription: This is how the item ends up in {file}

model.noMatchingFile: No matching file found. Allowed are .bbmodel, .json (+ PNG) and .png.
model.unreadable: The model could not be read.
model.onlyFirst: Only the first model was used.
model.noneDescription: Without a model the item looks like its base material ({material}).
model.dropSubtitle: Blockbench project (.bbmodel), Java model (.json) with PNG textures, or PNG textures
model.removeMessage: The model and its textures will be removed from the item.
model.requires: This model requires at least Minecraft {version}.
model.requiresTooHigh: This model requires at least Minecraft {version} – your project is set to {project}.
model.ambientOcclusionHelp: Soft shadows in corners and edges (ambientocclusion). Off for flat or glowing models.
model.shadeOverride: The model uses shade_direction_override (from Blockbench) – please change it there.
model.shadeSome: Directional shading of the cubes (shade) – off for {off} of {total} cubes.
model.shadeHelp: Directional shading of the cubes (shade). Off = all sides equally bright.

variants.title: Special Item Appearance
variants.empty: Pulling, Charged, Blocking, Cast, Throwing, Damaged, Dyeable, Composite or a custom GUI Model: add more models via Add.
variants.wrongMaterial: Only works with the material {materials} – currently {material}.
variants.dropManySubtitle: Multiple files at once – they are sorted by file name (e.g. bow_0, bow_1, bow_2).

slots.connectableHelp: Identical furniture next to each other connects, e.g. chairs into a sofa. Missing parts show the main model.
slots.placementsHelp: A different model depending on whether the furniture is placed on the floor, on a wall or on the ceiling.
slots.lightsHelp: Toggled item model: model while the light is switched on by right-click (light sources under “Mechanics → Furniture → Lights”).
slots.statesHelp: States you cycle through by clicking, e.g. a TV with channels. More settings under “Mechanics → Furniture → States”.
slots.nameInvalid: Only letters, numbers, _ and - are allowed.

recipes.title: Recipes
recipes.empty: No recipes yet. Use Add to define how this item can be crafted.
recipes.cookingTime: Cooking time in ticks ({seconds, number} s)
recipes.exportHint: Recipes are exported to {path} and loaded with {command}.

ceBlock.title: Block
ceBlock.description: CraftEngine places the item as a block of its own.
ceBlock.toggleHelp: The item places a custom block with the same ID.
ceBlock.toggleBlocked: The item places furniture. Turn off “Place as furniture” to make it a block.
ceBlock.autoStateHelp: CraftEngine shows the block through a free state of these vanilla blocks. The group decides the collision box: solid for full blocks, leaves for see-through blocks, tripwire for thin plants.
ceBlock.model: The block shows the item’s model. A flat item model becomes a cube from its textures: 1 texture on all sides, 2 as end and side (like a log), 3 as bottom, side and top.
ceBlock.behaviorHelp: What the block does. A behavior sets up the states it needs. For any other behavior, write it in the additional YAML under block: (for example block: behavior: type: falling_block).

states.template: The states come from CraftEngine’s template {template}. The behavior’s options above fill it in; the export adds the models from the item’s textures.
states.count: {count, plural, one {# internal state} other {# internal states}}, {appearances, plural, one {# appearance} other {# appearances}}. Each appearance takes one state of its group.
states.countUnknown: A property is incomplete, so the number of internal states is unknown.
states.propertiesHelp: CraftEngine makes one internal state for each combination of the values. Names like facing, axis and waterlogged get set on placement.
states.appearancesHelp: How the block looks. The first appearance is the default. Without a model path, an appearance shows the item’s model.
states.variantsHelp: Which appearance the block shows for property values, e.g. facing=north or open=true,facing=east. The first matching variant wins.

ceFurniture.title: Furniture
ceFurniture.description: CraftEngine places the item as furniture made of display entities, which can sit anywhere on a block.
ceFurniture.toggleHelp: The item places furniture with the same ID.
ceFurniture.toggleBlocked: The item places a block. Turn off “Place as a block” to make it furniture.
ceFurniture.variantHelp: Each variant is how the furniture looks when a player places it on top of a block, on its side or below it.
ceFurniture.variantMissing: The furniture has no variant here, so the item cannot be placed this way.
ceFurniture.previewHelp: The variant as placed in front of the player. Hitboxes are yellow, seats blue. Other blocks and texts show as grey blocks.
ceFurniture.rulesHelp: How the furniture snaps when a player places it.
ceFurniture.elementsHelp: What the furniture shows. An item display without an item shows this item’s model. Positions are in blocks from where the furniture stands.
ceFurniture.hitboxesHelp: Where players hit, use and sit on the furniture. Shulker and happy ghast hitboxes are solid, interaction hitboxes are not.
ceFurniture.settingsHelp: Behaviors, events and other keys go in the additional YAML under furniture:.
ceFurniture.lootHelp: Uses CraftEngine’s furniture loot. Other loot goes in the additional YAML under furniture: loot:.
